metaData.originalTitle: How Grab is Using AI Agents to Boost Team Productivity
metaData.title: How Grab is Using AI Agents to Boost Team Productivity
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Grab's data engineering team built a multi-agent AI system to automate answering repetitive data questions, reclaiming hundreds of engineering hours by shifting from reactive support to proactive work.
metaData.summary: This article details how Grab's Analytics Data Warehouse (ADW) team, overwhelmed by repetitive questions about their 15,000+ tables, built a multi-agent AI system to automate investigations. The system decouples the reasoning LLM (the brain) from specialized agents (the hands) that query data catalogs, trace code lineage, and check pipeline health. It features two pathways: a read-only investigation pathway with four agents (Classifier, Data, Code Search, On-call) and a Summarizer, and a semi-automated enhancement pathway for write operations that requires human approval. The article candidly discusses production challenges like context overflow, tool bloat, risky code execution, and user trust, detailing the solutions implemented. The system now handles most standard inquiries autonomously, reducing resolution time by an order of magnitude and freeing up significant engineering bandwidth.

mainPoints.point: Decouple the reasoning LLM (brain) from specialized execution agents (hands) for better debuggability and maintainability.
mainPoints.explanation: This separation allows the team to pinpoint failures to either reasoning errors or tool interaction issues, making the system easier to debug and improve incrementally.

mainPoints.point: Use different architectural pathways for read-only investigations and write operations based on their risk profiles.
mainPoints.explanation: Read-only queries can run with lighter oversight, while any operation that modifies production data requires human gates and a semi-automated workflow to prevent accidental damage.

mainPoints.point: Production hardening is the most challenging and critical part of building a multi-agent system.
mainPoints.explanation: Grab faced issues like context overflow across agent handoffs, tool bloat degrading performance, and the risk of unsafe code execution, requiring multi-layered solutions like token tracking, tool simplification, and four layers of safety guards.

mainPoints.point: A deliberate feedback loop from human reviews is essential for continuous improvement.
mainPoints.explanation: Annotations from human reviews are used to create test cases, identify systemic issues, track quality metrics, and drive targeted improvements, preventing the system from stagnating at its initial quality level.

keyQuotes: Their design philosophy started with a clean separation, which they describe as decoupling the brain from the hands.
Read-only operations and write operations have fundamentally different risk profiles, so they deserve fundamentally different architectures.
The lesson is that tool design is an important engineering concern, and fewer well-designed tools outperform a large collection of generic ones.
The goal was never to replace engineers. It was to give them their time back.
